l1: Provide general information about the server or workstation being affected
What is the role of the machine if it is a server (file server, DC, application server)?
Is the machine a virtual machine or a physical machine?
Is only one machine affected or are several machines affected?
What is the name of the application or process that is having the issue?
l2: How do users work with that application (logging in to a server, connecting to a database, running locally)?
What is the behavior of the application (crashing, hanging, slow, unable to connect)?
How do they recover when the issue happens (wait, reboot, hard shutdown, kill program)?

l1: When did the problem first start occurring?
When did the problem last occur?
Is this the only machine showing this behavior or are there others?
How often has the issue occurred?
l2: How do they know the issue is happening (what symptoms do end users or admins see)?
Is it always the same symptoms? What is the same and what is different?
Is the issue gradual or sudden in onset?
Are there any associated events being logged in the event viewer?

l1: Check the status of the WinRM service on the affected machine
Run the command WinRM quickconfig to verify WinRM configuration
Telnet to the remote machine on ports 5985 and 5986 to test connectivity
Check the properties of the WinRM listener by running winrm enumerate winrm/config/listener
Compare the output of winrm get winrm/config with a working machine
Run sfc /scannow to check for system file corruption
Check health of component store by running DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
l2: Check the resultant set of policies for any restrictive WinRM communication policies
Delete and recreate the WinRM listener after noting the previous configuration
Check if PowerShell remoting is working using Enter-PSSession -ComputerName
Run winrm invoke Restore winrm/config to restore listener configuration
Test WinRM connectivity between machines by running winrm id -r <remote computer name>
Reproduce the issue and check Event Viewer logs (Application and Services logs- Microsoft-Windows-WinRM)

l1: Check event logs in Application and Services logs- Microsoft-Windows-WinRM
Collect gpresult output to review Group Policy settings
Collect system information using the systeminfo command
l2: Collect WinRM trace logs for detailed troubleshooting
Capture a network trace during WinRM connection attempts

winrm_connection_failure.title: WinRM connection fails or times out

steps.action: Check WinRM service status and configuration
Test network connectivity on ports 5985 and 5986
steps.expect: Ports blocked or firewall issues identified

steps.action: Run WinRM quickconfig and recreate listener
Test WinRM connection and monitor Event Viewer
